title: A plateau rule changes the eastward oxygen decline timing in seven North Pacific bands on sigma0 26.5
abstract: We tested the eastward timing of the North Pacific oxygen decline in published annual ship estimates. The original ramp rule requires four sampled years on each plateau. We recover all seven published midpoints and a longitude slope of 0.113 year per degree on sigma0 26.5. With two plateau years the slope is 0.019; with no count rule it is -0.016. The sign also changes on 26.4 and 26.6. A joint fit with regional widths and amplitudes gives no eastward improvement over a same-time decline. A conditional five-year wild block test does not reject that null (999 replicates, p=0.103). The plateau rule excludes late endpoints most strongly in sparse western records. This limits the use of a fitted 2 cm/s speed as a physical constraint. It does not dispute the oxygen loss or independent outcrop evidence. We add no raw observations. Annual aggregate errors, sparse cruises, response shape and the conditional null limit inference.

display.caption: The same annual oxygen series give different midpoint order when the plateau year count changes.
